Identity.History:
Han Xin was one of the greatest generals of the early Han period and played a decisive role in Liu Bang’s victory over Xiang Yu. According to traditional accounts, his early life was marked by poverty and humiliation, but his military talent eventually attracted the attention of Xiao He, who persuaded Liu Bang to give him high command. Han Xin soon proved exceptionally capable at large-scale maneuver, deception, logistics, and the rapid conquest of rival territories.
During the Chu–Han Contention, Han Xin conducted a series of campaigns that destroyed or subdued several competing kingdoms. His victories at battles such as Jingxing became famous examples of unconventional strategy, including his celebrated use of troops positioned with their backs to a river. By attacking through northern and eastern China while Liu Bang occupied Xiang Yu elsewhere, Han Xin altered the strategic balance of the war and helped encircle the Chu regime.
His success, however, also made him politically dangerous. After the founding of the Han Dynasty, Liu Bang reduced Han Xin’s rank and military authority amid suspicions that such a powerful general might rebel. Han Xin was ultimately accused of conspiracy and executed in 196 BCE, reportedly under the authority of Empress Lü and Xiao He. His tragic fate became a classic example of the precarious relationship between victorious generals and newly established monarchs.
